Lower-trust sources (agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br, healthpolicy-watch.news, nytimes.com) are present as corroborating news sources that explicitly cite MoH/PAHO figures. metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: [![](https://journalmbr.com.br/public/journals/1/pageHeaderLogoImage_pt_BR.jpg)]( https://journalmbr.com.br/index.php/jmbr/index ) # Análise epidemiológica da Dengue no Brasil: uma série histórica 10 anos (2014 - 2024) ## Authors * Sarah Correa Soler Albino Titz de Rezende UNICID <https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2691-1999> * Octávio Correa Soler Albino Pontifícia Universidade Católica (PUC Minas Gerais) ## DOI: <https://doi.org/10.70164/jmbr.v2i1.427> ## Keywords: Dengue, Epidemiologia, Série Histórica, Medicina Preventiva. ## Abstract the study analyzed dengue in Brazil from 2014 to 2024, using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) and government programs such as the Dengue Program and monitoring by the São Paulo government. Through descriptive statistical techniques, confirmed dengue cases, hospitalizations, and deaths were characterized, segmented by region, age group, and gender. Frequency tables, graphs, and maps facilitated the understanding of annual and regional trends and the geographical distribution of the disease. The analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel 365 (2023). The results show significant variations in the distribution of reported cases. The Southeast region predominated in notifications, particularly in 2015, representing 61.93% of cases, and in 2024, with an estimated 64.33%. The Midwest recorded a high incidence in 2018 (40.28%), while the Northeast stood out in 2022, with 32.43% of cases. The South showed growth in cases starting in 2022, reaching 25.86% in 2023. These regional fluctuations highlight the need for specific preventive approaches. The high incidence and recurrent outbreaks pressured the public health system, underscoring the need to strengthen dengue control strategies.

metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: ![](https://www.apm.org.br/wp-content/uploads/logo-apm-95-anos.png) ##### Pesquisa # Ministério da Saúde divulga novos dados da dengue e demais arboviroses Boletim Epidemiológico demonstra que impactos do El Niño contribuíram para alta no número de casos ![](https://www.apm.org.br/wp-content/uploads/aedes-3.jpg) A nova publicação do [Boletim Epidemiológico](https://www.gov.br/saude/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/epidemiologicos/edicoes/2024/boletim-epidemiologico-volume-55-no-11.pdf/view) da Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente – órgão parte do Ministério da Saúde – traz informações sobre os casos de dengue, Chikungunya e Zika registrados entre 2023 e 2024. Segundo o documento, os impactos climáticos ocasionados pelo El Niño contribuíram para o aumento no número de casos suspeitos, principalmente nas Américas – região responsável por mais de 90% das notificações. Neste sentido, dados da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) demonstram que, até abril de 2024, foram contabilizados mais de 7,6 milhões de casos suspeitos de dengue ao redor do mundo e mais de 3 mil óbitos. Além do Brasil, que normalmente possui a maior proporção de casos no continente americano, México, Paraguai e sub-região do Caribe também tiveram aumento significativo nas notificações. No País, a variação de casos passou de 63%, em 2020, para 84%, em 2022. Em 2024, entre a primeira e 26ª semana epidemiológica, houve 6.215.201 notificações de dengue no Brasil, com coeficiente de incidência de 3.060,7 casos por 100 mil habitantes. Comparando com o mesmo período em 2023, os números representam um aumento de 344,5% nos casos registrados. O Sudeste foi a região com o maior coeficiente de incidência, registrando 4.739,8 casos por 100 mil habitantes.

metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: INFORME EPIDEMIOLÓGICO DENGUE, CHIKUNGUNYA E ZIKA NÚCLEO HOSPITALAR DE EPIDEMIOLOGIA/HNSC-HCC 1 INTRODUÇÃO A Dengue, Chikungunya e Zika são arboviroses urbanas transmitidas pelo mosquito Aedes aegypti. metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: ![](https://www.scielo.br/media/images/rsbmt_logo.png) # Open-access The greatest Dengue epidemic in Brazil: Surveillance, Prevention, and Control ![Open-access](https://ds.scielo.org/img/logo-open-access.svg) ## ABSTRACT In this review, we discuss dengue surveillance, prevention, and control measures in Brazil. Data on dengue epidemics between 2000 and 2024 indicates an increase in the number of dengue cases and deaths. Global climate change is a key driver of this growth. Over the past 25 years, nearly 18 million Brazilians have been infected with the dengue virus, and the highest number of dengue cases in Brazil's history is projected to reach 2024. Dengue mortality in Brazil increased geographically over time. As of June, there were approximately 6 million probable cases and 4,000 confirmed deaths in Brazil, which represents the greatest dengue epidemic to date. Several technologies have been developed to control *Aedes aegypti*, including the deployment of *Wolbachia*-infected mosquitoes, indoor residual spraying, sterile insect techniques, and mosquito-disseminated insecticides. The Ministry of Health recommends integrating these technologies into health services. Brazil is the first country to incorporate the Takeda vaccine into its public health system, and the Butantan vaccine is currently undergoing Phase 3 clinical trials. Increasing the vaccination coverage and implementing novel *Ae. aegypti* control technologies could reduce the number of dengue cases in Brazil in the coming years. Community activities such as home cleaning and elimination of potential mosquito breeding sites, facilitated by social media and health education initiatives, must continue to achieve this reduction.
